st: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then soak it in water for 20 minutes and drain well.
Heat [[0.25 cup]] oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the sliced onions for 8 minutes until deep golden.
Add the lamb, [[4 clove]] garlic, [[5]] cardamom pods and the cinnamon stick. Brown the meat on all sides for 6 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften into a thick sauce.
Pour in [[3.5 cup]] hot water, cover and simmer on low for 35 minutes until the lamb is tender (at least 145°F/63°C inside).
Stir the drained rice and [[0.25 cup]] raisins into the pot. Bring to a boil, then taste the liquid and add salt if needed.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork and serve with the lamb on top.
Cut the beef into small cubes about 0.5 inch wide so they cook fast. Pat them dry with paper towels.
Toss the beef with [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[0.5 tsp]] black pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a wide skillet over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer and sear for 4 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper. Cook for 5 minutes until the onion is soft.
Stir in the garlic and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] cumin. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 6 minutes until they break down and the pan is mostly dry. The beef should be cooked through with no pink.
Stir in the cilantro, taste, and adjust salt. Serve hot with rice, flatbread or pasta.
In a large bowl, whisk together [[1.5 cup]] flour, [[0.5 cup]] sorghum flour, [[0.5 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tsp]] sugar and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Pour in [[2.5 cup]] warm water and whisk until the batter is smooth and thin, like heavy cream.
Cover with a towel and leave at room temperature to ferment for 8 hours or overnight, until bubbly and slightly sour.
Stir the batter gently. If it is thicker than cream, whisk in a splash of water.
Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and rub it with a little of the [[1 tbsp]] oil on a paper towel.
Pour a small ladle of batter and swirl to make a round about 7 inches wide. Cook for 2 minutes without flipping until the top is covered in tiny holes and set.
Slide the canjeero onto a plate. Do not flip it. Repeat with the remaining batter, re-oiling the pan lightly now and then.
Serve warm with sugar and butter or sesame oil for breakfast, or with stew.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[0.5 cup]] warm milk, [[0.25 cup]] of the oil and about [[0.5 cup]] warm water. Mix and knead for 8 minutes until the dough is smooth and soft.
Cover the dough and rest it for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Roll one very thin into a large round, brush with a little of the remaining oil, and fold it up like an envelope or roll it into a rope and coil it.
Repeat with all the balls, then cover and rest them for 15 minutes so the layers relax.
Roll each coil or square out flat to about 7 inches wide, keeping the layers intact.
Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Cook one flatbread for 2 minutes per side, brushing with a little oil, until golden with brown spots.
Cook the rest the same way. Scrunch each hot bread gently with your hands to open the layers and serve warm.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, garlic and chili. Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the cilantro.
Spread the filling on a plate and let it cool completely, about 20 minutes. Hot filling will tear the pastry.
Mix [[1 tbsp]] flour with [[2 tbsp]] water to make a thick paste for sealing.
Cut each wrapper in half to make strips. Put a spoonful of filling at one end and fold the corner over into a triangle, then keep folding along the strip like a flag. Seal the end with the paste.
Heat [[3 cup]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry 4 or 5 sambusas at a time for 3 minutes, turning once, until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with a squeeze of lime or hot sauce.

ing: cut into chunks, bone-in is fine
st: Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the lamb and brown it for 6 minutes, turning the pieces.
Stir in the garlic, [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 4 minutes until they soften.
Pour in [[6 cup]] water and bring to a boil. Reduce to low, cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the lamb is nearly tender.
Add the potatoes and carrots. Simmer for 20 minutes more until the vegetables are soft and the lamb reaches at least 145°F (63°C).
Taste and add salt if needed. Stir in the cilantro and serve hot in bowls with flatbread or rice.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and garlic. Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F (71°C).
Stir in [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until a thick, saucy sauce forms.
Meanwhile, boil the spaghetti in well-salted water for 10 minutes or as the package says, then drain, saving a little cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if it looks dry.
Serve with a peeled banana on the side to bite between mouthfuls, and lime wedges to squeeze over.
Whisk [[2 cup]] cornmeal, [[1 cup]] flour, [[1 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1.5 cup]] warm water and [[1 tbsp]] oil. Mix and knead for 5 minutes into a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 hour until puffy.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and put a baking sheet inside to heat up.
Divide the dough into 6 balls and flatten each into a round about 0.5 inch thick, 5 inches wide.
Brush the rounds with some of the remaining oil and set them on the hot baking sheet.
Bake for 12 minutes, flipping once halfway through, until golden and firm with a few brown spots.
Split the hot muufo open or crumble it, drizzle with oil or butter and serve with stew or sugar and sesame oil.
Lightly grease a shallow dish or tray with [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Whisk [[1 cup]] cornstarch with [[1 cup]] of the water in a bowl until no lumps remain.
In a heavy pot, bring [[1.5 cup]] sugar and the remaining [[2 cup]] water to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Reduce the heat to low and slowly pour in the cornstarch mixture while stirring constantly with a wooden spoon.
Add [[0.25 cup]] of the melted butter and keep stirring for 15 minutes. The mixture will turn thick and glossy.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] cardamom and [[0.5 tsp]] nutmeg, then add the remaining butter a little at a time, stirring 15 more minutes until it pulls away from the pot.
Scrape the xalwo into the greased dish and smooth the top. Cool for 30 minutes to set.
Cut into squares and serve with coffee or tea.
Put [[2 cup]] water, [[4]] crushed cardamom pods, the cinnamon stick and [[3]] cloves in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes so the spices flavor the water.
Add the tea bags and simmer for 2 minutes until the water is dark.
Pour in [[2 cup]] milk and add [[3 tbsp]] sugar. Heat until steaming and just about to boil, stirring.
Let it bubble gently for 2 minutes, watching so it does not boil over.
Strain into cups, discarding the spices and tea bags. Taste and add more sugar if you like.
